verdict.line: You lose if you walk into three stacks of Acquired Taste and eat the follow-up stun at range; you win if you land your level 2-5 all-in before Tahm's Q poke chips you down.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Fury passive turns his W (Ruthless Predator) into a 1.5s triple-slash stun once he's above 50 Fury, and his E (Slice and Dice) dash lets him close the gap on a champion with zero mobility tools of his own. Tahm Kench's only answers are a 900-range Q (Tongue Lash) poke and a reactive W (Abyssal Dive) knockup, neither of which stop a committed all-in once Renekton is in his face. The 56% head-to-head win rate over 216 games and the solo-kill advantage both point to Renekton's burst windows outpacing Tahm's poke-and-shield plan.

theirWindow.what: The next Tongue Lash stuns you and consumes the stacks, so back out of his 900-range Q window before he lands the third hit, or he gets a free follow-up trade.

yourWindow.when: Fury above 50 and E/W off cooldown
yourWindow.what: Dash in with E (Slice and Dice) for the armor-shred, then W for the empowered triple-slash and 1.5s stun — this chain does high damage and shield-destroys before his E (Thick Skin) can convert banked damage into a shield.

start.why: The sustained auto-attack damage and healing let you trade into Tahm's early Q pokes without losing the lane-sustain war (58.1% WR, 83.4% pick).

boots.why: Tahm deals magic damage on his Q, passive, and ultimate — the magic resist directly blunts every source of his damage (58.4% WR, 71.7% pick).

core.why: The shield and burst proc reward the all-in pattern this matchup is built around.
Armor shred stacks with your empowered E's own armor reduction, letting your autos and W chunk through Tahm's tanky build faster (59.3% WR on this path over 27 games).
Converts the damage you take trading into Tahm's Q and autos into delayed damage you can heal through, keeping you alive for repeat all-ins.

situational.when: you're ahead and want to survive his Abyssal Dive knockup engages in extended fights
you're stacking Fury through repeated W/E resets and want the cooldown reduction to chain all-ins faster

runes.keystoneWhy: Tahm fights you in extended trades thanks to his Thick Skin sustain, so the stacking adaptive damage from Conqueror rewards staying in the fight rather than a single burst window.

summoners.why: Ignite's burn cuts through Tahm's Thick Skin heal and his Q self-heal, denying the sustain that would otherwise let him out-trade your all-in (56.1% WR, 85.5% pick).

playing.title: Hold the all-in until level 2
playing.detail: OP.GG's own data flags this: don't engage Tahm before level 2, since his Q range and slow punish a premature trade while you're still farming.

playing.title: Track your Fury bar constantly
playing.detail: Above 50 Fury, W becomes a three-hit, 1.5s stun that destroys shields — time your all-ins to land after you cross that threshold, not before.

playing.title: Use E to close, not just to poke
playing.detail: Slice and Dice's dash is your only way to force a fight on a champion with no mobility; save it for the engage rather than farming resets.

playing.title: Back off at 3 Acquired Taste stacks
playing.detail: Three Tongue Lash hits set up a stun on the fourth — disengage from his 900-range Q window before he can land it for free.

playing.title: Chain W into E for the stun-lock
playing.detail: Lead with the empowered W stun, then E in to maximize armor-shred uptime before his E (Thick Skin) shield absorbs the follow-up.

playing.title: Use R to extend trades after level 6
playing.detail: Dominus's periodic Fury gain keeps your W empowered through a longer fight, which matters since Tahm's Thick Skin rewards him for surviving short trades.

playing.title: Don't facetank Q poke on cooldown
playing.detail: Each Tongue Lash heals Tahm if it connects — dodge or trade back immediately rather than absorbing repeated pokes while waiting on your own cooldowns.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the matchup reasoning, timing windows, and trade patterns are my own tactical read built on top of that data.
